producer_report.summary: Retrying a retry now carries the original request. `earlier_attempt` follows "try again on <id>" requests back to the first request that is not a retry and puts that text in a new `original_request` field. The reader brief prints it under "That request was itself a retry. The original request:". B's findings still appear. A single retry gives the same brief as before, because the field is `None` when the rejected job is not itself a retry. The three error cases (unknown job, non-rejected job, bare "try again on") are unchanged. The walk keeps a visited-job set, and a code comment says so. It also stops, keeping the last request found, at a bare, unknown, or request-less reference. The original request goes through the same redactor call as the rest. I added a lifecycle test for the A→B→C chain. It puts a token built at run time in A's request and checks that the brief has the original request and B's findings, with the token redacted. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] has a new Fixed entry. Nothing for review 1 or the design was touched.

checks_run.note: all tests pass, including the new retrying_a_retry_carries_the_original_request_redacted and the existing retry and refusal tests

open_issues: No cycle test: a cycle among records cannot be created through `ask` (a job's reference must name an already-existing job), so loop protection (the visited set) is not exercised by a test.
Review 1 and the design revision remain unanswered, as the user's reply specified.
mistakes: My first shell calls used grep, which the producer policy denies; I switched to the Grep tool.
learnings: Retry detection lives in reading.rs `earlier_attempt`; I split the prefix parsing into `retry_reference` so the chain walk reuses it.
EarlierAttempt is built only in reading.rs, plus once in a briefs.rs unit test.
Redactor::redact_all takes a slice and replaces secret-shaped tokens with [secret:github-pat].
